So I made the jump over from smoking cigarettes to vaping, I started with the Aspire K1 starter kit. I've been reading a bit here and there and would appreciate any tips or tricks. I found a local shop that makes it's own organic juices and started with a regular tobacco flavor as well as a blueberry.

Hello! I've been vaping for close to a year now, and these are some things that I would recommend.

  1. get an extra battery. I looked up the K1 kit, and it looks like it only comes with one battery. If this is the case, I would recommend another battery or even two just so you always have a battery charged. If money permits, you might even consider buying a second kit, since a second tank is nice to have in order to easily switch up flavors.

  2. find a juice you like, and keep some on hand. Exploring new juice flavors is fun, but speaking from first hand experience, spending your entire vape budget on flavors that you don't like sucks if you don't have something to fall back on. I've made this mistake more than once, and now I just order my favorite flavors in larger sizes to make sure I have something I like. I never place an order or walk out of a vape shop without something that I know I like.

  3. Generally, i consider anything more expensive than $15 for a 30 ml bottle is too expensive. I will occasionally break this rule myself if I buy the juice from a shop, since I don't have to pay for shipping, and depending on the juice.

  4. Always keep some spare coils on hand as well. While i think those should probably last you at least a week, if not two, it's just another safety measure to make sure you don't have a poor vaping experience. When buying those coils, make sure they are for your tank specifically. Aspire makes BVC coils for various different tanks, such as the nautilus and i think the Atlantis. These will not be compatible with your tank. looking online, it look like you should look for "BVC Clearomizer replacement coils."

  5. Don't let a shop employee pressure you into anything like a mechanical mod/RDA/whatever. I don't know your shop, but I have heard stories of some shops doing just that.

Overall, I would like to point out that these are my personal experiences. People might disagree with me on a few points, so don't take my opinions as facts. Also, sorry if this seems like a lot. Things are actually pretty straight forward. It's like 3 am here I'm a little sleepy.

I'll take a look around for a spare battery, the one I've been using has lasted about a day and a half to almost two full days during the week. I did snag a second tank though it leaks a little, it seems like another Cleanomizer but with a different atomizer and tube setup. I'm going to try to return it or figure out the problem at the shop. I tried another atomizer with it but it still leaked out both tanks take the "BVC Cleanomizer replacement coils". I just took a look at Mount Baker Vapor for flavors and will snag a few of the larger bottles of flavors I've tried out, I almost made the mistake you did about buying multiple flavors that I may not have liked.

As far as heavy modding they did show off a bit at the shop I was at and said that "You'll be dripping in a month" and I honestly don't see that happening for awhile if ever. I think it's cool that mods like that are being done, but I don't see that being it being something I'll get into. The cool thing about that shop is the large amount of testers they have out, and I did get to see the production area they had where they make all their juices. It was pretty neat.

So far my short personal experience is great though, I haven't really touched analog cigarettes since I started and haven't had the major urge too. I still get a craving here or there but nothing serious. Thank you for sharing your experiences though, I appreciate answers responses like this. It sounds kind of silly, but I've never been able to pour soup from a can without splashing, no matter how much I tilt the bowl or the can.

If you first place the bowl over the open can upside-down, then flip them over together, the soup won't escape. When you lift up the can, the air pocket at the top of the can will force all of the contents out, so you don't need to scrape out every last chunk.
LPT: Don't pour soup into a bowl. Instead, place the bowl over the can, then flip both over. You won't spill, and the suction from the can will suck out every bit of the soup.
